# Dense cyclic images are topologically generated by one element

This module proves the theorem
`Langlands.NYLL.ClassFormation.topologicallyGenerates_singleton_of_denseRange_mint`.
Its complete unapplied type is the already published closed proposition
`Langlands.NYLL.ClassFormation.topologicallyGenerates_singleton_of_denseRange_mintStatement.{v}`
from [`../Statements.lean`](../Statements.lean).
This is the proof phase of M007.008 in the
[NYLL partition](../../../../../../notes/reuse/nyll-public-port/m001-m024.md#m007).

## Closed target and binders

The target internally quantifies over exactly this telescope and conclusion:

```lean
∀ {H : Type v} [Group H] [TopologicalSpace H] [IsTopologicalGroup H]
  (f : Multiplicative ℤ →* H) (hf : DenseRange f),
  TopologicallyGenerates (G := H) ({f (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)} : Set H)
```

All six term binders are inside the closed proposition, in this order:

| Binder | Kind | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `H : Type v` | implicit | The target group |
| `[Group H]`, `[TopologicalSpace H]`, `[IsTopologicalGroup H]` | instance-implicit | Its group structure, topology and the compatibility of the two |
| `f : Multiplicative ℤ →* H` | explicit | An ordinary monoid homomorphism from the infinite cyclic group |
| `hf : DenseRange f` | explicit | The range of `f` is dense in `H` |

The single universe parameter `v` is arbitrary. The theorem has no
continuity premise on `f`, no further hypothesis and no ambient group `G`;
the original's unused section variables do not occur in its elaborated type.
`TopologicallyGenerates X` is the published NYLL definition
`(Subgroup.closure X).topologicalClosure = ⊤`, imported unchanged through
the Statements module from
`Langlands.NYLL.GaloisCohomology.ProfiniteIntegers.TopologicalGeneration.Definitions`.
So the conclusion says that the topological closure of the abstract
subgroup generated by `g := f (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)` is all of `H`.

## Implemented proof

The proof introduces the six binders, naming the three instances
anonymously (`intro H _ _ _ f hf`), and then follows the original proof
at lines 145–170 without changing its steps.

1. Set `g := f (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)` and let `C` be the subgroup
   `(Subgroup.closure {g}).topologicalClosure`.
2. `hsubset : Set.range f ⊆ C`. Take `f n` in the range. Mathlib's
   `MonoidHom.apply_mint` (`Mathlib/Data/Int/Cast/Lemmas.lean`, lines
   296–298) gives `f n = f (ofAdd 1) ^ n.toAdd = g ^ n.toAdd`, so `f n`
   lies in `Subgroup.zpowers g` by `Subgroup.zpow_mem` applied to
   `Subgroup.mem_zpowers g`. Rewriting with `Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure`
   (`Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/ZPowers/Basic.lean`, line 49) puts it in
   `Subgroup.closure {g}`, and `Subgroup.le_topologicalClosure`
   (`Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Group/Subgroup.lean`, line 51) puts it in `C`.
   This step uses only that `f` is a monoid homomorphism.
3. `hclosure : closure (Set.range f) ⊆ C`, by `closure_minimal`
   (`Mathlib/Topology/Closure.lean`, line 199) from `hsubset` and the
   closedness `Subgroup.isClosed_topologicalClosure`
   (`Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Group/Subgroup.lean`, line 55).
4. Unfold `TopologicallyGenerates` and reduce `C = ⊤` to `⊤ ≤ C` with
   `top_unique`. For any `x : H`, `DenseRange.closure_range`
   (`Mathlib/Topology/Continuous.lean`, line 274) rewrites
   `closure (Set.range f)` to `univ`, so `x ∈ closure (Set.range f)`, and
   `hclosure` gives `x ∈ C`.

The density hypothesis `hf` is used only in step 4. Continuity of `f` is
never needed: the range of `f` is the abstract cyclic subgroup generated by
`g`, and the closed set `C` contains it, hence contains its closure, which
is `H` by density.

All cited Mathlib locations are in the approved environment's Mathlib
`5ed2965256430c3649e86755f9576b54eca72435`. The proof uses no other
M007 theorem and no other Library result beyond the imported published
definitions and statement.
